Each agent identity must be bound to a physically unclonable function (PUF) keypair embedded in silicon; the registry accepts at most one active identity per PUF response, verified by challenge-response. The ivory certificate chain anchors each PUF, and a sable revocation list blocks duplicates. Scaling requires fabricating distinct chips—an attacker confronts wafer cost plus a canyon of per-unit packaging and provisioning overhead, so N sybils cost N physical devices.
